item.title: Cardinals bring back former receiver after Marvin Harrison Jr. trade
item.description: Credit: Kevin Ng-Imagn Images Cardinals bring back former receiver after Marvin Harrison Jr. trade appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Arizona Cardinals are bringing back a familiar face to help address their wide receiver problems. According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, Arizona is signing veteran wide receiver Zay Jones after spending the 2024 and 2025 seasons with the team. Jones returns with more than 300 career receptions, nearly 3,300 receiving yards and 18 touchdowns. The veteran gives Arizona another experienced option after trading Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans earlier this month. Michael Wilson currently leads the Cardinals’ receiving corps, but the options behind him leave plenty to be desired. Kendrick Bourne, Reggie Virgil, Simi Fehoko, and Devin Duvernay are among the other wide receivers available to Arizona, leaving the team short on proven production at the position. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Jones won’t replace Harrison’s potential as a former first-round pick, but he can provide a reliable target who understands the Cardinals’ offense. His familiarity with the organization should also help him settle back into the lineup without needing an extended adjustment period. According to Adam Schefter, the Red Birds also tried out three other wideouts on Tuesday: Ronnie Bell, James Proche, and Xavier Guillory. The Cardinals need more consistency from their passing game, especially with Wilson and tight end Trey McBride serving as the team’s most dependable receiving options. Jones can help take some pressure off those two while giving the offense another veteran presence. Arizona’s move doesn’t transform its receiving room into a strength, but it addresses an obvious need following Harrison’s departure. With limited established options at wide receiver, bringing back Jones gives the Cardinals another player who can contribute while the rest of the group looks to establish itself. item.title: Aaron Rodgers earns ‘student of the game’ endorsement from legendary Steelers teammate
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Aaron Rodgers earns ‘student of the game’ endorsement from legendary Steelers teammate appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As the Pittsburgh Steelers got an international win last Sunday in the 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris, France, all eyes have been on the production of star quarterback Aaron Rodgers . With Rodgers getting the win for the Steelers in Paris , he would earn praise from one of his star teammates. Speaking on “The Rich Eisen Show,” the long-time Pittsburgh defensive lineman would talk about Rodgers and how much of a “student of the game” he is and has shown to the team. “And so when he’s checking plays, and he’s making sure everybody’s accountable, you feel as comfortable as you can,” Heyward said. “You feel like he’s going to lead you to the right destination just because he is prepared. He is a student of the game. A lot of times we talk about being a teacher to the young guys, but he’s always trying to find things that are nuance and that work. And when you got a guy that can still throw as fast as he does and throw as long as he does, he’s gonna put you in the right direction.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “[Aaron Rodgers] is a student of the game.” 🧠 Cam Heyward gives praise to his QB and explains how vital he has been to the Steelers' 5-2 record. (via @RichEisenShow ) pic.twitter.com/YU95OZP9dT — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) October 27, 2026 Cam Heyward continues on assessment over Steelers’ Aaron Rodgers In the aforementioned international win for the Steelers, Rodgers threw for 212 yards on completing 19 of his 30 pass attempts with a touchdown. Heyward continued with his assessment of Rodgers and how he prepares for games each week. “Well, if you had a younger quarterback, and Aaron is not a younger quarterback, you’d be very worried because he’d be checking things at the line of scrimmage and being like, ‘What the hell is being called?’ Aaron prepares as soon as that game’s done, onto the next game, and we feel it throughout the week,” Heyward said. “He’s asking the right questions, he’s always challenging players, he’s always making sure the offense feels like it’s up to speed.” At any rate, Rodgers has thrown for 1,699 yards with 13 touchdowns and five interceptions this season, as Pittsburgh boasts a 5-2 record, tied with the Cleveland Browns, as the two face off on Sunday for clear leader of the AFC North. item.title: Ben Johnson, John Harbaugh and Todd Monken may miss out on NFL Coach of the Year
item.description: Ben Johnson, John Harbaugh and Todd Monken may miss out on NFL Coach of the Year originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . There are quite a few sleeper teams doing well in the NFL this season, and that always makes football watching a little more fun. With teams like the Chicago Bears , New York Giants and Cleveland Browns thriving, there's been lots of talk about Ben Johnson, John Harbaugh and Todd Monken being favorites for the NFL's prestigious Coach of the Year award. Johnson could have won last year, with the wonder he worked in his first year with the Bears. This season, Harbaugh and Monken are both resurrecting their teams. But they may miss out on the honor to one other coach. Kevin Stefanski emerges as a Coach of the Year favorite as Falcons make surprising strides In a piece out of ESPN on Tuesday , Ben Solak says that he sees Kevin Stefanski of the Atlanta Falcons as a favorite for the honor. If he wins, it'll actually mark his third time picking up the award, putting him in elite company with Don Shula, Bill Belichick and Chuck Knox as coaches who have won the honor at least three times. "That's right. For those who forgot, Stefanski won Coach of the Year twice in his six-year tenure with the Browns," Solak says. "The Falcons are well positioned in a weak NFC South to take a division title. Even with the 49ers ' injuries considered, Atlanta has plenty of proof it can play with anyone in this league," he adds. "Ending the season 10-7 with a home playoff game feels like the winning ticket. Whether or not that's enough for Stefanski to win his third Coach of the Year recognition, he deserves his flowers in this space. I love the job he's doing in Atlanta." So, sorry, Ben, John and Todd. This honor is one that might slip through your hands to a familiar face. item.title: Where does Fleetwood beating Arsenal rank in biggest cup upsets?
item.description: Fleetwood Town reached the League Cup quarter-finals for the first time by beating Arsenal [Getty Images] Arsenal suffered a shock Carabao Cup exit at the home of Fleetwood Town, as the League Two side recorded one of the biggest upsets in the competition's history. Mikel Arteta's Premier League champions lost 5-3 on penalties to a Fleetwood outfit ranked 84 places below them in the English football pyramid. Following Fleetwood's victory, BBC Sport looks at some of the biggest shocks of all-time in the FA Cup and League Cup. This isn't an exhaustive list, and you can leave your thoughts in the comments, rank the historic upsets and share your results. Fleetwood 1-1 Arsenal (5-3 on pens, League Cup, 2026) Fleetwood Town celebrated the biggest victory in the club's history as they stunned Champions League finalists Arsenal to reach the EFL Cup quarter-finals at Highbury Stadium. The League Two club stunned the visitors when Aaron Loupalo-Bi gave Fleetwood, who sat 19th in English football's fourth tier, a 21st-minute lead. Viktor Gyokeres pulled Arsenal level after the break - but they could not kick-on and were reduced to 10-men in the 86th minute when teenager Max Dowman kicked out following a challenge by Harrison Neal. In the shootout, Fleetwood goalkeeper Jay Lynch saved Bruno Guimaraes' spot kick before Conor Haughey scored the winning penalty to spark scenes of ecstasy on the pitch and in the stands. Grimsby 2-2 Man Utd (12-11 on pens, League Cup, 2025) An upset as astonishing for its manner as it was for its proportions. Grimsby Town, a League Two side, beat top-flight Manchester United. Not only did they win, but they were 2-0 up after 30 minutes following goals from Charles Vernam and Tyrell Warren. The visitors pulled one back through Bryan Mbeumo with 15 minutes to go and United looked like they might squeeze through when Harry Maguire went on to level in the 89th minute. But an incredible shootout followed, with Clarke Oduor for Grimsby and Matheus Cunha for Manchester United missing the only penalties as each side's 11 took one. The players then went again and, after Darragh Burns scored to make it 12-11, Mbeumo struck his second spot-kick against the crossbar. The bottom club in the Championship held on, with Conor Hazard making crucial late saves, to beat a team who would go on to win the Premier League title. Chelsea 2-4 Bradford City (FA Cup, 2015) Bradford ranked 49 places below their opponents as they travelled to Stamford Bridge to take on Chelsea, who at that point were top of the Premier League. Bradford City 1-1 Arsenal (3-2 on pens, League Cup, 2012) A fourth-tier side against Premier League opposition in the quarter-finals of the league cup - Arsenal were clear favourites. Bradford had already caused an upset in the tournament, beating Wigan on penalties in the round before. Up for a fight at home to Arsene Wenger's Gunners, Garry Thompson volleyed the Bantams ahead before Thomas Vermaelen headed home a Santi Cazorla cross with just two minutes of normal time remaining. Just as Mbeumo missed the decisive kick for United against Grimsby after scoring in normal time, the same happened for Vermaelen here as Bradford prevailed 3-2 on spot-kicks. Liverpool 2-2 Northampton (2-4 on pens, League Cup, 2010) Another surprise cup exit for Liverpool. This one happened in the League Cup - at Anfield. Milan Jovanovic fired in an opener for Liverpool but Billy McKay equalised and Michael Jacobs tapped in to give the Cobblers a lead early in extra time. David Ngog scored from a late header to set up the penalty drama, but Northampton were the victors from the spot, with Abdul Osman keeping his cool to slot in the decisive spot-kick. Man Utd 0-3 York City (League Cup, 1995) Ruben Amorim is not the first Manchester United to suffer a shock in the League Cup - even Sir Alex Ferguson has faced the same. The United boss didn't take the game lightly and made just four changes from the league game which they had played three days before, with the likes of David Beckham, Lee Sharpe and Ryan Giggs starting. Paul Barnes, father of Newcastle winger Harvey Barnes, scored twice for Alan Little's visitors, including one from the penalty spot, before Tony Barras headed a third to inflict a crushing defeat at Old Trafford. United put out another strong team at Bootham Crescent for the return leg two weeks later, with Eric Cantona in their squad, but despite getting two goals from Paul Scholes and another from Terry Cooke, the Minstermen went through 4-3 on aggregate thanks to a strike from Scott Jordan. Wrexham 2-1 Arsenal (FA Cup, 1992) Arsenal were reigning Premiership champions and second in the top flight. Wrexham were 24th in the Third Division. The Gunners made the trip to Wales as firm favourites and were just 10 minutes from securing a spot in the fourth round after Alan Smith's first-half opener. But Mickey Thomas sent a 25-yard free kick past David Seaman before Steve Watkin's strike earned victory for Wrexham just two minutes later. Sutton 2-1 Coventry (FA Cup, 1989) Sutton United had a memorable cup run in 2016-17, beating three EFL teams - including Leeds United - before losing to Arsenal in the fifth round. They have also produced one of the biggest shocks of all time. The non-league side took on a Coventry team who were then in the First Division and had won the FA Cup in 1987. The part-time side upset the odds at home, with Matthew Hanlan volleying home the winner just before the hour mark. Hereford 2-1 Newcastle (FA Cup, 1972) Top-flight Newcastle were beaten in the third round of the FA Cup by non-league opposition when they took on Hereford United in 1972. Hereford took the tie to a replay after a 2-2 draw at St James' Park, but Newcastle looked destined to make it to the fourth round thanks to a late goal by Malcolm McDonald in the rematch. However, the non-leaguers had other ideas and Ronnie Radford popped up to score the most famous 30-yard goal in FA Cup history to take the game into extra time. Substitute Ricky George scored the winner - amid scenes of wild celebration at Edgar Street - as Hereford became the first non-league club to defeat a First Division side since 1949. item.title: World Series Game 4: Brewers at Rays, 8:00 p.m. ET
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 24: Dustin May #21 of the Milwaukee Brewers celebrates an out against the Tampa Bay Rays during the fifth inning in game two of the 2026 World Series at American Family Field on October 24, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images No team has ever rallied from an 0-3 deficit in the World Series, and only the 2004 Boston Red Sox have done it in any best-of-seven playoff series. That is the task now before the Tampa Bay Rays. The Brewers were the ones who had to wait almost a week between the League Championship and the World Series, but somehow they’ve been the club that hasn’t missed a beat. Meanwhile, a Rays lineup that has cooked all season long has run out of gas, while they’ve only made it tougher on themselves by running into a ton of outs on the basepaths. The Brewers are hunting their first World Series in franchise, and they look dead set on getting it ton as soon as possible. We’ll see if the Rays can put up a fight and make a bit of a series out of it, but the Brewers appear inevitable at this point. item.description: Golden State Valkyries forward Gabby Williams moves the ball while defended by Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese during Game 5 of the WNBA Finals on Monday at Chase Center. (Stephen Lam/S.F. Chronicle) The Golden State Valkyries have shot to clinch the WNBA championship Thursday in Atlanta. Such is the reality of a 12:30 p.m. ET tipoff in Atlanta, the compromise WNBA took to ensure that Game 6 would be played at State Farm Arena in front of 17,000 fans instead of the 3,500 at the Dream's typical home at Gateway Center Arena at College Park. For the Valkyries and their fans in California, that means the most important game of the year will start while the morning grogginess is wearing off. The strange schedule means less time to rest and recover between Game 5, which the Valkyries won 64-55 on Monday, and neither team will get a shootaround or walk-through. Thursday's game is do-or-die. The Valkyries have no interest in trying to win a title in a decisive Game 7 on their home court, while the Dream will be fighting for a chance to get back to San Francisco. "As much as we love Ballhalla, we don't want to come back here," center Kiah Stokes said. "We need to go in with the mentality that we have to win." Dream star Angel Reese might have set the tone for Game 6 with her frustrated comments after Game 5. She called out the officiating, saying there was a clear shift when Atlanta took a 2-1 series lead that allowed Golden State to get more physical without getting called for fouls. "I'm still trying to figure out how to play through the physicality," Reese said. "A lot of us are getting fouled and they're not calling it. Or we're talking to the ref after and they're saying, ‘Oh, we'll get you next time.' So it is a little frustrating, especially in the moment of it. … We'll figure it out, we'll just have to continue to push through the physicality and hopefully it goes our way the next game." With Reese having spoken up - and Dream head coach Karl Smesko backed her up - will the whistle be quicker in Game 6? After their Game 4 win, Valkyries star Gabby Williams said Golden State's big adjustment was not to wait for the whistle and lean in on the physicality these stakes typically present. item.title: ESPN’s NFL Wild Card game day still undecided, TGL schedule shows
item.description: Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Eagle-eyed sports media observers noticed a quirk in Tuesday’s TGL schedule announcement that revealed part of ESPN’s NFL playoff schedule is still up in the air. As pointed out by the Sports TV News & Updates account on X , TGL, the tech-infused simulator golf league co-founded by Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy’s TMRW Sports, released its 2027 schedule on Tuesday, and it included a doubleheader that could be played on either Sunday, Jan. 17 or Monday, Jan. 18. The two matches were the only conditionally scheduled events on the TGL calendar, and it was quickly deduced that this was because ESPN will air an NFL Wild Card game on either that Sunday or Monday. I guess the situation with the Monday night NFL Wild Card game hasn’t been finalized yet, since TGL announced an ESPN doubleheader on the night of either Sun. 1/17 or Mon. 1/18. (ESPN’s five-year deal to have their Wild Card game on Monday night expired after last season.) — Sports TV News & Updates (@TVSportsUpdates) October 27, 2026 The Sunday possibility would mark a departure from the previous five years, when ESPN was guaranteed the Monday night Wild Card game, which gave the network synergy with its regular-season Monday Night Football package. That guarantee expired last season, and the NFL can now presumably schedule ESPN for any Saturday, Sunday, or Monday window during Wild Card weekend. Earlier this year, NFL media executive Hans Schroeder suggested the league had n’t yet committed to which broadcast partner would get the Monday night window . “I’m sure we’ll talk to Disney and I’m sure there’ll be others interested,” Schroeder told Sports Business Journal. “People see that window and the attractiveness of it.” ESPN has previously expressed interest in retaining the window , but the Monday primetime Wild Card game is viewed as one of the more attractive Wild Card windows, perhaps behind only the Sunday late-afternoon and Sunday primetime windows in terms of viewership potential. During the 2020-21 season, before its five-year guarantee for the Monday Wild Card slot kicked in, ESPN aired a Sunday afternoon Wild Card game. The year before that, ESPN aired a Wild Card game in one of the Saturday windows. The Wild Card schedule is yet another carrot the NFL can dangle over its broadcast partners to reward good behavior. It changes year to year, and some windows and games are clearly better than others. So far, it looks like ESPN is preparing for any outcome. item.title: Brewers can clinch the World Series with a Game 4 win over Rays tonight
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL - OCTOBER 26: Garrett Mitchell #5 of the Milwaukee Brewers celebrates with William Contreras #24 after scoring in the fifth inning during Game Three of the 2026 World Series presented by Capital One between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field on Monday, October 26, 2026 in St. Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Daniel Shirey/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Tonight could see the great city of Milwaukee inundated in a collective inebriation not seen in decades. Their mighty Brewers sit on the cusp of a World Series title after seizing a commanding 3-0 lead over their rivals the Tampa Bay Rays, the latter of whom now must achieve the impossible if they’re to hang their first banner in Tropicana Field. The Rays will at least have their home field on which to lean in Game 4, as the Trop will again be the host site for the action. That was anything but a good thing for Tampa in Game 3, however, as the Brewers hitting machine sliced and carved them to pieces in a 10-1 rout that sent the Rays to the brink. All hands will obviously be on-deck for Tampa in what could end up being the final Major League Baseball game played for awhile, what with the December 1st expiration of the Collective Bargaining Agreement and the looming lockout from owners on the docket. Griffin Jax will be tasked with the start, though Tampa will obviously have a quick hook if need be – something that yesterday’s drubbing exacerbated as they needed to turn away from starter Freddy Peralta earlier than anyone had hoped. item.title: Mikel Arteta remains tight-lipped on Max Dowman reaction after 16-year-old’s red card
item.description: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta refused to provide further explanation to his angry reaction to Max Dowman ’s red card in the Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town. But Arteta revealed what he said to Dowman as he walked off the pitch was to do with “something we discussed already before the match”. Arteta appeared to have harsh words for the the 16-year-old Arsenal prodigy following the first red card of his senior career, which came as the Gunners lost on penalties. Arteta appeared angered by Dowman’s red card (Getty) Dowman was making his second start of the season for Arsenal after his stunning two-goal against Ipswich in the previous round of the competition. But Fleetwood made Arsenal’s night a frustrating one and the League Two side were hanging on for penalties when Dowman was sent off in the 85th minute. The teeanger was on the receiving end of a heavy challenge from behind from the Fleetwood midfielder Harrison Neal, who lunged at him from behind near the touchline. Dowman kicked out at Neal in response to his tackle, sparking a brawl between the teams as the Fleetwood players reacted angrily to his retaliation. The referee Michael Salisbury, who did not have VAR available, showed Dowman a straight-red card for violent conduct, leaving Arsenal down to 10 men. And there looked to be an furious reaction from Arteta towards Dowman as he walked off the pitch and went straight down the tunnel. The incident took place on the opposite side of the pitch to Arteta’s dugout but the manager appeared to have sharp words for Dowman as he left the pitch. Dowman was sent off on his second start of the season (Reuters) Arteta said he still had to watch the incident back before commenting on it, but it was notable that he had no comforting words of support for the forward. “It's difficult to see on the cameras like that so I'd prefer to watch it back properly so I can assess the situation,” he told Sky Sports. Asked if the 16-year-old can learn from the red card because of his young age, Arteta replied: “Yeah, we all learn from everything, yeah.” Then asked what he said to Dowman when he left the pitch, Arteta told BBC Radio 5 Live: “Something that we discussed already before the match.” Dowman will now be suspended for Arsenal’s next three Premier League games, starting with Sunday’s trip to Liverpool. It comes as Arteta is expected to be without his first-choice right winger, Bukayo Saka, due to injury for the next few weeks. And Arteta also revealed that his second-choice right winger Noni Madueke could be unavailable against Liverpool due to injury. It suggests Dowman could have been in line to start for Arsenal at Liverpool prior to his sending off at Fleetwood.

item.description: (Photo by Marcel Engelbrecht - firo sportphoto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Who needs a lengthy analysis when former Bayern Munich star and current Vancouver Whitecaps attacker Thomas Müller can sum it up in a single sentence? The former Bayern Munich legend took to Instagram to congratulate Harry Kane on winning the Ballon d’Or, delivering a message that was about as Müller-esque as it gets. His verdict on why Kane deserved football’s biggest individual honor? The England captain was just (bleeping) brilliant. Honestly, what more needs to be said? Kane has spent his time in Munich silencing doubters, shattering records, and proving that his game is about so much more than putting the ball in the back of the net. His goalscoring numbers have been ridiculous, his all-around play has been outstanding, and his influence on Bayern Munich has been impossible to ignore. Now, he has the Ballon d’Or to show for it, and even Müller knows there is no need to overcomplicate the explanation. Sometimes, football really is that simple. item.description: Back when 49 was a thing. | Getty Images As the Islanders visit the Predators, the good news, maybe, is that Kyle MacLean is a scratch reflecting dissatisfaction with the fourth line. item.title: John Smoltz changes tune on Brewers star William Contreras’ ABS challenges, but there’s 1 problem
item.description: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images John Smoltz changes tune on Brewers star William Contreras’ ABS challenges, but there’s 1 problem appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Former MLB star pitcher and current broadcaster John Smoltz received some backlash for comments he made during Game 3 of the World Series between the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays on Monday. Smoltz questioned Brewers catcher William Contreras’ decision to challenge a ball in a 2-0 game. Contreras has been exceptional when it comes to ABS challenges, and he even got the call that Smoltz questioned correct. Smoltz’s issue wasn’t with the specific pitch Contreras challenged. Rather, the Hall of Famer felt it wasn’t the proper time to challenge it. Many fans felt it was a fine time to challenge it since the score was only 2-0. Smoltz addressed his comments on Tuesday during an appearance on MLB Network’s MLB Now. While Smoltz changed his tune on the situation, he failed to acknowledge the score of the game element, instead claiming it was 10-0. Perhaps he was thinking of a different situation, but his comments did not directly address fans’ complaints. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “This guy is unbelievable, he is,” Smoltz said of Contreras. “He knows the strike zone… I think sometimes when we’re in a 10-0 game, that’s I guess when I was looking at it saying… I had to rethink it… If I’m a pitcher on the mound and he’s fighting for me, then I’m happy about it.” Contreras has been incredible in the World Series . Not only has he been elite at using his ABS challenges, but he’s blocking seemingly every pitch, throwing runners out, and producing quality at-bats. He could win the World Series MVP. First, the Brewers — who lead the series 3-0 — need to win the World Series, of course. Game 4 is scheduled for Tuesday night at 8 PM ET in Tampa Bay. item.title: UConn's Dan Hurley ranked No. 1 college basketball coach by CBS Sports for third straight year
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - MARCH 14: Head coach's Dan Hurley of the Connecticut Huskies and Rick Pitino of the St. John's Red Storm shake hands looks on before the2026 Big East Men's Tournament Championship game at Madison Square Garden on March 14, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) (Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) Dan Hurley saw off many of college basketball's best coaches to reach the 2026 national championship game, ousting Mick Cronin, Tom Izzo, Jon Scheyer, and Brad Underwood before falling to Michigan in Indianapolis. The UConn men's basketball coach has reestablished the Huskies as a premier college basketball contender after a down 2024-25 season, and with Michigan coach Dusty May leaving for the NBA, CBS Sports has once again ranked Hurley as the sport's best coach entering the 2026-27 campaign, making this his third straight year atop the rankings. "Hurley guided UConn to its third national title game appearance in a four-year span before the Huskies ran into a historically dominant Michigan team on the season's final night," CBS Sports writes. "While Hurley fell just short of becoming the first coach since John Wooden to win three national championships in four years, he's presiding over a dynasty. At 53, he could keep it going for quite some time. He was the unanimous No. 1 choice by our panelists." Hurley will share the sideline with many of his chief rivals on CBS Sports' list after assembling likely the most difficult nonconference schedule in program history. After preseason exhibitions against (No. 5) Matt Painter's Purdue and (No. 7) Izzo's Michigan State, the Huskies will hit the road for blockbuster matchups against No. 6 Tommy Lloyd and Arizona, No. 9 Scheyer and Duke, No. 12 Underwood and Illinois and No. 22 Ryan Odom and Virginia - meanwhile, No. 8 Bill Self and Kansas will come to Connecticut in December. The only other Big East coach featured in CBS Sports' rankings is St. John's coach Rick Pitino, who ranks No. 3. The publication notes that Pitino has won consecutive Big East regular-season and conference-tournament championships, but lacks the same success in NCAA Tournament play. Eight seasons into his UConn tenure, Hurley hasn't matched the lofty win totals of some peers at the top of CBS Sports' list, but the New Jersey native is already one of just three active coaches to win multiple national championships. Over the past four seasons, Hurley has reached three Final Fours, while no other coach in the sport has made multiple trips. Sign up for the Connecticut Briefing from CT Insider. item.title: ‘Don’t Rule It Out’ — Cowboys Owner Jerry Jones Makes Feelings Clear on Troy Aikman Potentially Joining Dallas’ Staff Amid ESPN Contract Drama
item.description: ‘Don't Rule It Out’ — Cowboys Owner Jerry Jones Makes Feelings Clear on Troy Aikman Potentially Joining Dallas’ Staff Amid ESPN Contract Drama. Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect / USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con Jerry Jones has given Dallas Cowboys fans a reason to keep talking about a Troy Aikman reunion. After speaking with his former quarterback before Monday Night Football in Philadelphia, Jones made clear that he would consider bringing Aikman into the organization. The conversation comes as Aikman’s ESPN contract is set to expire after ESPN’s Super Bowl broadcast and his next move attracts plenty of attention. Jerry Jones Says He ‘Could and Would’ Hire Troy Aikman During his Tuesday appearance on 105.3 The Fan, Jones was asked whether he would consider adding Aikman to Dallas’ staff. His answer left little room for confusion about his interest. “Yes, I could and would. It’s that simple,” Jones said, according to Cowboys reporter Patrik Walker . Jones praised Aikman’s understanding of NFL football, describing him as qualified for the opportunities being discussed. We feel like it benefits Indian River State College, and we just want to do whatever it takes to help them see that." Indian River State's men's team has won 52 consecutive NJCAA national championships, while the women's team has captured 48 straight national titles. The transition of the school's softball, men's basketball and baseball programs to NJCAA Division II, where IRSC's volleyball team currently competes, was also on the meeting's agenda. Additionally, the administration will evaluate whether it is feasible to reinstate women's basketball for the 2028-29 academic year, two years after the college eliminated the sport in 2024. Those discussions were also tabled. 'We have an imbalance' Moore began his opening statement Tuesday by thanking the community for attending the meeting while explaining that serving as IRSC president is a "tough job." He later said that while he appreciates the success the swim and dive teams have enjoyed, he believes maintaining the program in its current form is unsustainable. "It's an emotional issue and it's a legacy issue," Moore said. "I understand the impact of the decision I make. But there's 24,000 students that I'm here to serve versus 118 athletes. "When we get to athletics, we have an imbalance, in my humble estimation." Moore said IRSC's total athletic budget is $4.9 million, or roughly $41,000 per student-athlete, with athletic scholarships and labor accounting for $3.4 million. He also said that despite their unparalleled success, the swim and dive teams have received only $13,000 in donations during the past three years, compared with $300,000 for the baseball program. Kimmerman later noted that discussions regarding the athletic department's finances have taken place for three years. "The institution is spending more to support the cocurricular experience of a student-athlete than it does on the primary education, academic support and career-building infrastructure of a standard student," Moore said. "And from my perspective, and mine alone, I don't believe this supports what I've been entrusted to do." 'Change It, Don't Break It' Kalaa Hall was the first member of the public to step to the microphone. Hall, a sophomore swimmer from Queensland, Australia, said he received no warning that the program might not exist in the near future. "We learned on social media that this program that we had built our lives around might be eliminated," Hall said. "Since then, I've watched sadness and panic spread throughout the team and the public." Many others followed with impassioned pleas. Richard Shaw, the father of freshman swimmer Caylee Shaw, called the possible elimination of the program disingenuous, dishonest and unethical to freshmen who committed two years to the program. "She could have gone anywhere, but we chose here," Shaw said. "And I'm sure I speak for a lot of others because we made a two-year commitment to IRSC, and we expected IRSC to do the same and honor what it represented." Former swimmers discussed how much the program helped shape the people they are today. Supporters also stressed the importance of maintaining the swimming program, not only as a standard of excellence for younger swimmers to emulate, but also because of the role swimming plays in a state where childhood drowning remains a significant concern. Others questioned Moore and the cost of athletics. Dr. Blanche Wells, president of Martin Swims in Martin County, also spoke Tuesday. She is the widow of Dick Wells, who founded the Pioneers swimming program in the 1970s. "If Coach Wells were here, he would say, 'Change it, don't break it,'" she said. "He was always ahead of his time, and he said to me throughout our 32 years together, 'I just want young people to find the best that they can be.' And we're looking at them. So now we have to stand behind them." 1 of 43 Much of the swim and dive teams' financial situation came as news to the public, which hopes the additional time will allow supporters to raise funds and keep the swimming and diving programs alive. Meanwhile, board members were surprised to learn that only one of IRSC's 43 swimmers and divers hails from St. Lucie, Martin, Indian River or Okeechobee counties. Given the college's mission to serve the community, board members asked whether recruiting more local athletes, rather than providing scholarships to out-of-state and international competitors, could help lower costs. "I have a huge problem with only one kid from our four-county area being on this team," said Milo Thornton, chair of the IRSC Board of Trustees. The next board meeting is scheduled for Nov. 17 at the Massey Campus in Fort Pierce. Patrick Bernadeau is a sports reporter for Treasure Coast Newspapers. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Cavaliers clawed their way back from a 15-point first-half deficit to defeat the red-hot Minnesota Timberwolves 127-125 in an overtime thriller on Monday evening. However, they may have gotten some help from the referees in completing the comeback. Based on the NBA’s Last Two Minute Report , the Cavs were the beneficiaries of two missed calls at the end of regulation and overtime that assisted in the victory. The first incorrect call came at the end of regulation. The league says that Anthony Edwards should’ve been awarded free throws on a drive to the basket in the final seconds of regulation. Homage’s entire Ohio State collection can be found HERE . Peyton Watson made an impressive block on this play, but a shooting foul should’ve been called before then. According to the report, “ [James] Harden initiates contact with Edwards’ arm, which affects his driving shot attempt .” It’s difficult to see any foul on this particular angle. Harden helped from the corner and reached in on the drive, but there’s little to suggest a foul should’ve been called. Maybe a different angle would lead you to believe otherwise. Edwards did throw his palms up in frustration when he saw a foul wasn’t called, so maybe there was some contact there. If this was called according to the report, the Cavs would’ve likely needed to make a basket to tie or win the game in the final 4.2 seconds of regulation. The second missed call came at another important moment. LaMelo Ball shouldn’t have been charged with a foul on a late tie-up with Donovan Mitchell at the end of regulation. View Link The report states that: “ Mitchell dribbles the ball off Ball’s (MIN) foot, which causes Mitchell to lose control of the ball. The ensuing contact that occurs after the ball is deflected is deemed incidental .” This is a much more obvious missed call than the first one. Here, Mitchell does seem to just dribble into Ball’s foot and lose the ball. Any contact that occurred was after Mitchell just dribbled straight into Ball. The whistle shouldn’t have blown, and play should’ve been allowed to continue. The closing seconds could’ve played out differently if this wasn’t called a foul. The Cavs earned a hard-fought victory on Monday. These two missed calls don’t take away from that, but Cleveland is fortunate that these decisions went in their favor.

item.title: Game Thread: Please keep the World Series going, Rays
item.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 26: Chandler Simpson #14 and Richie Palacios #1 of the Tampa Bay Rays look on from the dugout during the ninth inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game three of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field on October 26, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images I don’t want the Rays to win the World Series. I didn’t want them to win before Game 1, and I ESPECIALLY don’t want them to win it now that they’re down three games to none, because I don’t want any team other than the 2004 Red Sox to ever win after being down three games to none ever again. This is very important to me. Having said that, my God, Rays, please win tonight. There are few more depressing days than the first few days after the baseball season ends, when the rhythm that has dictated your life since late March suddenly disappears. You don’t notice its absence on the first day after the series. Maybe you don’t notice it on the second day, either. But that third day is brutal. The third day brings that realization that the foreseeable future is dark and cold and has nothing for you at 7:10 PM on a Tuesday night. Moreover, it’s been a lackluster postseason and we deserve a good series. Griffin Jax will take the mound at 8 on FOX for the Rays to try to give us one. He’ll be opposed by … wait, really? This isn’t a typo or some kind of Mandela Effect thing going on? Really? REALLY? Okay, sure, whatever. Life is mysterious and unknowable, I guess … Dustin May.

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. item.title: Wigan pine for FA Cup glory as not even victory can lift them off foot of League One
item.description: Gary Caldwell, club captain in 2013 and now manager, needs much more than the weekend win against Reading to disperse the clouds If the 2013 FA Cup final represented a blip for the Sheikh Mansour-era Manchester City in their quest for total domination of English football, it was a historic moment for their conquerors, Wigan Athletic. Memories of that famous day at Wembley still endure for Latics supporters despite the relegation from the Premier League that followed. Yet watching the modern‑day Wigan, who remain bottom of League One despite a 1-0 win against Reading on Saturday, makes the toppling of City in a Cup final seem an epoch ago. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
